message.content:
You are working in the repo /Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final (BMW hackathon: AI app that turns BMW customer feedback + product/sales data + web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements). Read AGENTS.md first (rules), then foundation/documents/data-inventory.md (sections 2, 3, 4 describe exactly the files you will parse) and skim src/bmw_req/db.py, src/bmw_req/ingest/feedback.py, src/bmw_req/ingest/reference.py, src/bmw_req/llm/client.py (the ONLY allowed path to OpenAI).

YOUR TASK: build deterministic ingest for the three remaining BMW datasets, plus tests, then run them on the real data.

Hard rules:
- Raw data in `challange information document/BMW-Data/` is read-only and confidential: never modify/move/commit it; never send it anywhere except OpenAI via `bmw_req.llm.LLM`.
- Use `uv run ...` for everything (Python 3.12 venv). openpyxl for xlsx (no pandas in app code). `pdftotext -layout` (homebrew) is available for PDFs.
- Do NOT edit foundation/STATE.md, DECISIONS.md or OPEN_QUESTIONS.md (the lead agent does that). Do NOT commit. Do NOT change the schema in db.py except by APPENDING entries to the `MIGRATIONS` list if you truly need a new column (another agent works in parallel; keep db.py edits minimal). Tables `study_metric`, `sales`, `source_item` (incl. new column `wave`), `ingest_batch`, `audit_event` already exist — use them.
- Every ingest creates an `ingest_batch` row and an `audit_event` (actor_type 'system', like feedback.py does). Idempotent: re-running must not duplicate rows (source_item has UNIQUE(kind, ref)).
- Markets/models are data, not code paths (AGENTS rule 7) — keep mappings in small config dicts at module top.

1) `src/bmw_req/ingest/study.py` — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`
   - Sheet `CN_EU_2025`: label row followed by `Mean` row per category; columns China → BMW 5 Series G68, BMW 7 Series G70; EU → BMW 1 Series F70, BMW 5 Series G60, BMW 7 Series G70. Inspect the sheet layout yourself first (print the first ~15 rows) — don't trust my description blindly.
   - Sheet `US_2025`: per question a block `Sample total` + 7-point distribution (I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It) for G60 and G70. Compute top2 = Delightful + I Love It, bottom3 = I Hate It + A Failure + Unsatisfactory, net = top2 − bottom3, and a mean on 1..7.
   - One `source_item` per (item × model × market): kind='study', trust_tier='T1', vehicle_model_id (G68 for 5 Series China, G60 for 5 Series EU/US, F70, G70), market_code, ref like `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx#CN_EU_2025:R12:C4` (sheet + excel row/col of the value), text = a readable sentence e.g. "Customer study 2025, BMW 5 Series G68 (China) — Seating comfort: mean 8.43 (scale unconfirmed, Q-006; no sample size)", meta_json with all numbers + raw label + sheet, wave=2.
   - One `study_metric` row per source item: scale 'mean_10' (CN/EU) or 'dist_7' (US); fill mean/top2/bottom3/net; z_within_column = z-score of the item's mean (CN/EU) or net (US) vs the other items in the same model×market column; rank_within_column (1 = worst) and n_items_in_column.
2) `src/bmw_req/ingest/sales.py` — `sales_volumes.xlsx` (sheets F70, G60_G68, G70; columns market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030). Inspect it first. G60_G68 sheet: CN row → vehicle G68, other markets → G60. One source_item kind='sales', T1, per sheet row, meta_json notes "values look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015) — use as BMW-internal relative weights". Insert `sales` rows (year 2024, 2025, 2030 with is_forecast=1 for 2030). Map the file's market codes onto our market table codes (EU/US/CN/RoW); print what codes the file uses. wave: the 2024 figures belong to wave 1 and 2025/2030 to wave 2 — simplest: store two source_items per row (one for 2024 with wave=1, one for 2025+2030 with wave=2), each with its own ref suffix (e.g. `#G60_G68:R3:2024`), and point the sales rows at the matching source_item.
3) `src/bmw_req/ingest/options.py` — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF` (German price lists). Use `pdftotext -layout` per page. Then use the cheap model to turn the equipment sections (Serienausstattung = standard equipment, Sonderausstattungen = options, packages like M Sportpaket / Pakete) into structured items. Use `bmw_req.llm.LLM().generate(job='ingest:options:<model>', tier='fast', schema=<pydantic model>, reasoning_effort='low', flex=True, max_output_tokens=..., instructions=..., input=...)` per page or per group of pages. Each item: name_de, name_en (translation), category (one of: Exterior, Interior, Comfort & Space, Infotainment & Digital, Driving Experience, Powertrain (as experienced), Range & Charging, Driver Assistance (as experienced), Variants & Packages, Design & Quality Perception — import `Category` from bmw_req.pipeline.extract), availability ('standard' | 'optional' | 'package'), package_name (if part of a package), applies_to (model variants if the page says), price_eur (number or null; stored only as information — pricing/business case is out of scope), source_line (the exact line of the PDF text it came from). Verify source_line is a substring of the page text (whitespace-normalized); keep a `line_verified` flag. Skip pages that are pure technical data (Technische Werte), colours, or price tables of models unless they list equipment. Store one source_item per item: kind='option_list', T1, vehicle_model_id, market_code='EU' (German market list; for US/CN the equipment baseline is an assumption — say so in meta), ref like `G60_OptionList.PDF#p12:<slug>`, text = "<name_en> (<availability>, DE price list Jul 2026)", quote = source_line, wave=1. Budget: this must cost well under $0.20 total; the wrapper logs every call. Do a 1–2 page pilot first, inspect output quality, then run all pages. Dedupe identical items within a model.
4) Wire a CLI: `uv run python -m bmw_req.ingest.study`, `...sales`, `...options [F70 G60 G70]` (each module with a `main()`), and make `python -m bmw_req.ingest` keep working for feedback.
5) Tests in tests/test_ingest_data.py on SYNTHETIC files you build in tmp_path (no BMW data in tests, no paid calls; for options test only the deterministic parts like line verification / storage with a fake LLM result).
6) Run all three on the real data (`data/app.db` is the real DB; another process may be writing extraction results concurrently — the connection uses WAL + busy_timeout, keep transactions short with BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT). Verify counts against data-inventory.md (37 CN/EU categories, 103 US questions; per-column z-scores sane). Run `uv run pytest -q`.

Final report (concise, <= 40 lines): files created, row counts per table/kind, the market codes found in sales, any data surprises, option-list item counts per model + verified-line rate + total LLM cost (query llm_usage for job LIKE 'ingest:options%'), and any open issues.

# CLAUDE.md

@AGENTS.md

## Claude-specific notes

- `AGENTS.md` (imported above) is the canonical rule set shared with Codex and other agents — edit rules there, not here, so both stay in sync.
- The project memory is `foundation/` — read `foundation/README.md` for the read/write protocol. Prefer it over personal memory for anything project-related.
- The app's LLM provider is **OpenAI** (D-006) — don't add the Anthropic SDK or Claude model IDs to the app code.

# AGENTS.md

Hackathon project for the **BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"** challenge: an AI app that turns customer feedback, BMW product/sales data and web research into **prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements** for successor BMW vehicles, with a **product manager (PM) in the loop** and a **full audit trail**.

**Portfolio-level by design:** multiple models, markets, shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR → Neue Klasse) and plants from day one. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest example; F70 and G70 use the same pipeline. **LLM provider: OpenAI.** Stack: Python 3.12/uv, LangGraph, SQLite + sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit (D-015–D-020).

## Session start — mandatory

Read, in order (short):
1. `foundation/STATE.md` — phase, team, demo path, next steps, budget
2. `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check for blockers
3. `foundation/DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table at the top; open full entries only when relevant. Don't re-open settled decisions without new info.

Then read only what your task needs:

| If your task touches… | Read |
|---|---|
| Scope, deliverables, what BMW asked | `documents/challenge-brief.md` |
| BMW data files, counts, quirks | `documents/data-inventory.md` |
| Stack / tooling, budget guard | `documents/tech-stack.md` |
| Workflow, entities, audit rules | `documents/architecture.md` |
| Requirement fields, evidence levels, scoring | `documents/requirement-model.md` |
| Research agents, trust tiers, brand/feasibility checks | `documents/knowledge-base.md` |
| Platforms, plants, BMW sales (cited) | `documents/portfolio-reference.md` (long — search it) |
| Competitors, trends, brand guardrails (cited) | `documents/competitor-landscape.md` (long — search it) |
| BMW Group Report 2025: deliveries, EV share, R&D, NK, digital | `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` |
| Unknown term or code | `documents/glossary.md` |
| Fresh clone / setup | `foundation/README.md` → Fresh clone |

## Session end — mandatory

- Update `foundation/STATE.md` (phase, in progress, next up, one-line session log entry with date).
- Log every decision as `D-xxx` in `foundation/DECISIONS.md`; new questions as `Q-xxx` in `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.
- If code changes the stack, schema, or workflow, update the matching doc in `foundation/documents/` in the same change.

## Core rules

1. **Raw data is read-only and confidential.** `challange information document/` (typo is the real folder name) is git-ignored — never modify, move or commit it; never send it anywhere except the agreed LLM provider. Derived data goes to git-ignored `data/`.
2. **Stay in scope.** Customer-facing requirements only (features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital, design & quality perception, driving experience, range/charging as experienced, variants/packages). **Out:** regulatory/homologation, engineering/component specs, pricing/business cases (rough effort as a factor is OK).
3. **Traceability is non-negotiable.** Every finding links to ≥1 source item; every requirement links to ≥1 finding. Keep provenance (file, sheet, row/ID, URL + date for web).
4. **Evidence vs. assumption.** Always separate evidence-backed statements from forward-looking assumptions (3–5 yr horizon); surface conflicting evidence instead of hiding it.
5. **The PM decides, never the AI.** AI only creates/edits in `proposed` status; `approved`/`rejected`/`deferred` require a human actor + rationale. Exception (D-013): AI may recompute *scores* of any requirement (logged); priority/status changes stay proposals.
6. **Audit everything, append-only.** Every change to requirement content, score, priority, evidence or status → an `audit_event` (actor human/ai/system, timestamp, before/after, rationale, model for AI).
7. **Portfolio, not one-offs.** Brands, models, markets, platforms and plants are data/config — never hardcode a derivative or market. Requirements can target several derivative × market combinations.
8. **Brand & segment fit.** Every requirement must fit the brand and the segment (no "cheap efficiency hatch" from BMW, no budget Rolls-Royce). Brand-fit `fail` blocks approval unless a PM overrides with rationale.
9. **Plant & platform feasibility.** A recommendation must be buildable: the derivative's platform and a plant that builds it can serve that market in time (incl. Neue Klasse transition). Used as a feasibility filter only — never output engineering specs. Whether a `fail` blocks approval is open (Q-010: BMW lists "architecture" as out of scope).
10. **Web evidence is cited evidence.** Competitor, sales, demand and expectation facts come from web research with URL, publish/retrieve date and trust tier (T1–T3). LLM opinions are never stored as sources; unverified user claims stay flagged until verified.
11. **Explainable prioritization.** Every score has a visible factor breakdown and plain-language rationale.
12. **OpenAI for all LLM work**; model names via env (`OPENAI_MODEL_*`). Secrets live in `.env` (git-ignored); commit `.env.example` only.
13. **Markets are different customers.** Climate, usage and culture differ — segment findings by market and score/prioritize each derivative × market separately; surface cross-market conflicts (D-011).
14. **Future, not just past.** Derive what customers will need at successor launch (3–5 yr) from predecessor feedback + competitors + trends; tag horizon, Kano class and assumptions (D-012).
15. **Living process, not a one-shot list.** ~2-year process: every prioritization run is snapshotted; AI only *proposes* priority/status changes with their cause; PM decides; history is always visible (D-013).
16. **$100 OpenAI budget, total.** Cheap model (`gpt-6-luna`) for bulk extraction/classification/summaries; `gpt-6.1-sol` only for reasoning-heavy steps; all calls through the budget-guarded wrapper; Flex/Batch + caching; capped web-search calls; pilot before full runs; update the Budget section in `foundation/STATE.md` after paid runs (D-010, thresholds D-014).
17. **Don't decide architecture alone.** The stack is fixed in D-015–D-020; changing it (new framework, store, LangChain, …) needs the team first. The demo data model is open (Q-017).
18. **Hackathon pace.** Ship a working demo path end-to-end before polishing; prefer simple, cached, deterministic pipelines over clever ones. Don't build what's not needed for the demo.

## Quick facts

- Datasets per vehicle: verbatims (xlsx), customer study (xlsx, CN/EU means + US 7-point distribution), sales volumes 2024/25/2030 (xlsx), German option price list (PDF).
- Feedback xlsx has **one row per classification** — dedupe by `ID` when counting verbatims.
- No China verbatims exist; US verbatims dominate G60/G70 (90–95%); F70 has no US data but ~⅓ Japan; almost no EU verbatims for G70. No dates in feedback.
- BMW sales volumes look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015) — never blend them silently.
- Local anaconda Python is broken for pandas — use a `uv` venv (Python 3.12).

## Commits

Small, descriptive commits; don't commit unless asked. Never commit raw BMW data, `.env`, or local DBs.

def connect(path: Path | str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open the app DB (default `data/app.db`), load sqlite-vec and ensure the schema.

    Autocommit mode: callers open transactions explicitly (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
    """
    if path is None:
        path = get_settings().db_path
    if str(path) != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.enable_load_extension(True)
    sqlite_vec.load(conn)
    conn.enable_load_extension(False)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    _migrate(conn)
    return conn


# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition). CREATE IF NOT EXISTS
# doesn't add them to an existing DB.
MIGRATIONS = [
    ("signal", "llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("verbatim_extraction", "recheck_llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("signal", "support_question", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"),   # Q-020, D-024
    # Simulated ingest waves (Q-012, D-027): the wave in which an item becomes visible to the pipeline.

    ("requirement_target", "evidence_level", "TEXT"),

    ("requirement_target", "run_id", "INTEGER"),
    ("change_proposal", "kind", "TEXT"),            # priority | status | content | new_requirement | link_finding

def _migrate(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    for table, column, definition in MIGRATIONS:
        cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})")}
        if column not in cols:
            conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}")

                       WHERE e.source_item_id = signal.source_item_id AND e.extractor_version = signal.extractor_version)"""
                )

"""Ingest a `{derivative}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` file: one `source_item` per verbatim ID.

The raw file has one row per (verbatim × BMW classification); the labels are kept in meta_json as hints.
Idempotent: verbatims already ingested are skipped, and no batch is created if nothing is new.
"""

import json
import sqlite3
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

from bmw_req.ingest.reference import country_to_market

SHEET = "Feedback_Explorer"
ENGINE = {"BEVE": "BEV"}


def read_verbatims(path: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True)
    rows = wb[SHEET].iter_rows(values_only=True)
    header = next(rows)
    col = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(header)}
    verbatims: dict[str, dict] = {}
    labels = defaultdict(list)
    for excel_row, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        vid = r[col["ID"]]
        if vid is None:
            continue
        verbatims.setdefault(vid, {
            "id": vid,
            "source": r[col["Source"]],
            "country": r[col["Country"]],
            "derivative": r[col["Derivate (e-code)"]],
            "engine_raw": r[col["Engine Type"]],
            "text": r[col["Customer Feedback"]],
            "rows": [],
        })["rows"].append(excel_row)
        if r[col["Feedback Type"]] or r[col["Vfc level2 Name"]]:
            labels[vid].append({
                "feedback_type": r[col["Feedback Type"]],
                "vfc_level2": r[col["Vfc level2 Name"]],
                "vfc_level3": r[col["Vfc level3 Name"]],
                "vfc_level2_3": r[col["Vfc level2 3 Name"]],
            })
    wb.close()
    for vid, v in verbatims.items():
        v["bmw_labels"] = labels[vid]
    return verbatims


def ingest_feedback(conn: sqlite3.Connection, path: Path) -> int:
    """Returns the number of newly ingested verbatims."""
    path = Path(path)
    verbatims = read_verbatims(path)
    ref = lambda vid: f"{path.name}#{SHEET}:{vid}"
    existing = {
        r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT external_id FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'feedback' AND ref LIKE ?", (f"{path.name}#%",)
        )
    }
    new = [v for vid, v in verbatims.items() if vid not in existing]
    if not new:
        return 0
    market_of = country_to_market(conn)
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        batch_id = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO ingest_batch (kind, description, file) VALUES ('feedback_wave', ?, ?)",
            (f"{len(new)} verbatims from {path.name}", path.name),
        ).lastrowid
        conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
                                        country, text, meta_json, ingest_batch_id)
               VALUES ('feedback', ?, ?, 'T1', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [
                (
                    ref(v["id"]), v["id"], v["derivative"], market_of(v["country"]), v["country"], v["text"],
                    json.dumps({
                        "channel": v["source"],
                        "engine": ENGINE.get(v["engine_raw"], v["engine_raw"]),
                        "engine_raw": v["engine_raw"],
                        "excel_rows": v["rows"],
                        "bmw_labels": v["bmw_labels"],
                    }),
                    batch_id,
                )
                for v in new
            ],
        )
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value)
               VALUES ('system', 'ingest.feedback', 'ingest', 'ingest_batch', ?, ?)""",
            (str(batch_id), json.dumps({"file": path.name, "verbatims": len(new)})),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return len(new)
"""Minimal reference rows the ingest needs (D-021). Markets and models are config, not code paths
(AGENTS rule 7). Platforms, plants, production and market profiles come later from the cited seed docs."""

import json
import sqlite3

EUROPE = [
    "AT", "BE", "BG", "CH", "CY", "CZ", "DE", "DK", "EE", "ES", "FI", "FR", "GB", "GR", "HR", "HU", "IE",
    "IS", "IT", "LI", "LT", "LU", "LV", "MT", "NL", "NO", "PL", "PT", "RO", "SE", "SI", "SK",
]

MARKETS = [
    ("EU", "Europe", EUROPE),
    ("US", "United States", ["US"]),
    ("CN", "China", ["CN"]),
    ("RoW", "Rest of world", ["*"]),
]

BRANDS = [("BMW", "BMW", "BMW Group")]

# (id, brand, line, body)
VEHICLE_MODELS = [
    ("F70", "BMW", "1 Series", "hatchback"),
    ("G60", "BMW", "5 Series", "sedan"),
    ("G68", "BMW", "5 Series", "sedan, long wheelbase (China)"),
    ("G70", "BMW", "7 Series", "sedan"),
]


def seed(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO brand (id, name, brand_group) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", BRANDS
    )
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO market (code, name, countries_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
        [(code, name, json.dumps(countries)) for code, name, countries in MARKETS],
    )
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vehicle_model (id, brand_id, line, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", VEHICLE_MODELS
    )


def country_to_market(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> callable:
    """Build a country → market-code lookup from the `market` rows; '*' is the catch-all."""
    exact, fallback = {}, None
    for row in conn.execute("SELECT code, countries_json FROM market"):
        for c in json.loads(row["countries_json"]):
            if c == "*":
                fallback = row["code"]
            else:
                exact[c] = row["code"]
    return lambda country: exact.get(country, fallback)

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS source_embedding USING vec0(embedding float[1536]);
"""


def connect(path: Path | str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open the app DB (default `data/app.db`), load sqlite-vec and ensure the schema.

    Autocommit mode: callers open transactions explicitly (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
    """
    if path is None:
        path = get_settings().db_path
    if str(path) != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.enable_load_extension(True)
    sqlite_vec.load(conn)
    conn.enable_load_extension(False)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    _migrate(conn)
    return conn


# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition). CREATE IF NOT EXISTS
# doesn't add them to an existing DB.
MIGRATIONS = [
    ("signal", "llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("verbatim_extraction", "recheck_llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("signal", "support_question", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"),   # Q-020, D-024
    # Simulated ingest waves (Q-012, D-027): the wave in which an item becomes visible to the pipeline.
    ("source_item", "wave", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
    ("finding", "source_kind", "TEXT"),            # verbatim | study | web | reference
    ("finding", "polarity", "TEXT"),               # pain | want | like | context
    ("finding", "category", "TEXT"),
    ("finding", "first_wave", "INTEGER"),
    ("requirement", "effort", "TEXT"),             # S | M | L rough effort (prioritization only, no cost math)
    ("requirement", "must_not_lose", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"),
    ("requirement", "realization_note", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement", "created_by", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement", "first_run_id", "INTEGER"),
    ("requirement", "derivation_json", "TEXT"),     # raw AI draft incl. horizon_reason, cited IDs
    ("requirement_target", "evidence_level", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement_target", "proposed_priority", "TEXT"),   # AI proposal; `priority` is the PM-confirmed one
    ("requirement_target", "run_id", "INTEGER"),
    ("change_proposal", "kind", "TEXT"),            # priority | status | content | new_requirement | link_finding
    ("audit_event", "run_id", "INTEGER"),
]


def _migrate(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    for table, column, definition in MIGRATIONS:
        cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})")}
        if column not in cols:
            conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}")
            if (table, column) == ("signal", "llm_usage_id"):
                # Backfill: until D-023 every signal came from its verbatim's first-pass call.
                conn.execute(
                    """UPDATE signal SET llm_usage_id = (SELECT e.llm_usage_id FROM verbatim_extraction e
                       WHERE e.source_item_id = signal.source_item_id AND e.extractor_version = signal.extractor_version)"""
                )
"""`uv run python -m bmw_req.ingest [F70 G60 G70]` — seed reference rows and ingest feedback files."""

import sys

from bmw_req.config import get_settings
from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.ingest import reference
from bmw_req.ingest.feedback import ingest_feedback


def main(derivatives: list[str]) -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    conn = connect()
    reference.seed(conn)
    for d in derivatives:
        n = ingest_feedback(conn, settings.raw_data_dir / f"{d}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx")
        print(f"{d}: {n} new verbatims")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:] or ["G60"])
"""Ingest a `{derivative}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` file: one `source_item` per verbatim ID.

The raw file has one row per (verbatim × BMW classification); the labels are kept in meta_json as hints.
Idempotent: verbatims already ingested are skipped, and no batch is created if nothing is new.
"""

import json
import sqlite3
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

from bmw_req.ingest.reference import country_to_market

SHEET = "Feedback_Explorer"
ENGINE = {"BEVE": "BEV"}


def read_verbatims(path: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True)
    rows = wb[SHEET].iter_rows(values_only=True)
    header = next(rows)
    col = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(header)}
    verbatims: dict[str, dict] = {}
    labels = defaultdict(list)
    for excel_row, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        vid = r[col["ID"]]
        if vid is None:
            continue
        verbatims.setdefault(vid, {
            "id": vid,
            "source": r[col["Source"]],
            "country": r[col["Country"]],
            "derivative": r[col["Derivate (e-code)"]],
            "engine_raw": r[col["Engine Type"]],
            "text": r[col["Customer Feedback"]],
            "rows": [],
        })["rows"].append(excel_row)
        if r[col["Feedback Type"]] or r[col["Vfc level2 Name"]]:
            labels[vid].append({
                "feedback_type": r[col["Feedback Type"]],
                "vfc_level2": r[col["Vfc level2 Name"]],
                "vfc_level3": r[col["Vfc level3 Name"]],
                "vfc_level2_3": r[col["Vfc level2 3 Name"]],
            })
    wb.close()
    for vid, v in verbatims.items():
        v["bmw_labels"] = labels[vid]
    return verbatims


def ingest_feedback(conn: sqlite3.Connection, path: Path) -> int:
    """Returns the number of newly ingested verbatims."""
    path = Path(path)
    verbatims = read_verbatims(path)
    ref = lambda vid: f"{path.name}#{SHEET}:{vid}"
    existing = {
        r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT external_id FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'feedback' AND ref LIKE ?", (f"{path.name}#%",)
        )
    }
    new = [v for vid, v in verbatims.items() if vid not in existing]
    if not new:
        return 0
    market_of = country_to_market(conn)
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        batch_id = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO ingest_batch (kind, description, file) VALUES ('feedback_wave', ?, ?)",
            (f"{len(new)} verbatims from {path.name}", path.name),
        ).lastrowid
        conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
                                        country, text, meta_json, ingest_batch_id)
               VALUES ('feedback', ?, ?, 'T1', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [
                (
                    ref(v["id"]), v["id"], v["derivative"], market_of(v["country"]), v["country"], v["text"],
                    json.dumps({
                        "channel": v["source"],
                        "engine": ENGINE.get(v["engine_raw"], v["engine_raw"]),
                        "engine_raw": v["engine_raw"],
                        "excel_rows": v["rows"],
                        "bmw_labels": v["bmw_labels"],
                    }),
                    batch_id,
                )
                for v in new
            ],
        )
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value)
               VALUES ('system', 'ingest.feedback', 'ingest', 'ingest_batch', ?, ?)""",
            (str(batch_id), json.dumps({"file": path.name, "verbatims": len(new)})),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return len(new)
"""Minimal reference rows the ingest needs (D-021). Markets and models are config, not code paths
(AGENTS rule 7). Platforms, plants, production and market profiles come later from the cited seed docs."""

import json
import sqlite3

EUROPE = [
    "AT", "BE", "BG", "CH", "CY", "CZ", "DE", "DK", "EE", "ES", "FI", "FR", "GB", "GR", "HR", "HU", "IE",
    "IS", "IT", "LI", "LT", "LU", "LV", "MT", "NL", "NO", "PL", "PT", "RO", "SE", "SI", "SK",
]

MARKETS = [
    ("EU", "Europe", EUROPE),
    ("US", "United States", ["US"]),
    ("CN", "China", ["CN"]),
    ("RoW", "Rest of world", ["*"]),
]

BRANDS = [("BMW", "BMW", "BMW Group")]

# (id, brand, line, body)
VEHICLE_MODELS = [
    ("F70", "BMW", "1 Series", "hatchback"),
    ("G60", "BMW", "5 Series", "sedan"),
    ("G68", "BMW", "5 Series", "sedan, long wheelbase (China)"),
    ("G70", "BMW", "7 Series", "sedan"),
]


def seed(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO brand (id, name, brand_group) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", BRANDS
    )
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO market (code, name, countries_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
        [(code, name, json.dumps(countries)) for code, name, countries in MARKETS],
    )
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vehicle_model (id, brand_id, line, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", VEHICLE_MODELS
    )


def country_to_market(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> callable:
    """Build a country → market-code lookup from the `market` rows; '*' is the catch-all."""
    exact, fallback = {}, None
    for row in conn.execute("SELECT code, countries_json FROM market"):
        for c in json.loads(row["countries_json"]):
            if c == "*":
                fallback = row["code"]
            else:
                exact[c] = row["code"]
    return lambda country: exact.get(country, fallback)

# Data Inventory

All raw files: `challange information document/BMW-Data/` (read-only, git-ignored). Profiled 2026-10-10; re-verified 2026-10-10 (pandas 3 in a `uv` Python 3.12 env + openpyxl/pdftotext).

**Counting rule:** the feedback files have one row per (verbatim × classification). All verbatim counts below are **unique `ID`s** unless a column says "rows".

## 1. Customer feedback (verbatims) — `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Sheet `Feedback_Explorer`, 12 columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Verbatim ID, e.g. `G60-0001`. **Not unique per row** — one row per (verbatim × classification). An ID never spans two sources. |
| `Source` | Anonymized channel `Source A`–`D` (interpretation open, Q-005) |
| `Brand`, `Sales Description` | `[BMW]`, `[BMW 5 Series]` |
| `Country` | ISO-2 (US, GB, JP, KR, …) |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | F70 / G60 / G70 |
| `Engine Type` | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (= BEV; the raw value is `BEVE`) |
| `Feedback Type` | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, or empty (unclassified) |
| `Customer Feedback` | Free text, mean ~215–225 chars per verbatim (Source D ~125) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | Combined "Component : Issue" label |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | Component / topic (e.g. `Seats`, `Touch screen, operation`, `Electric Range`) |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | Issue type (e.g. `Not user-friendly`, `Like: function`, `Customer request: function`) |

| File | Rows | Verbatims (unique IDs) | Sources (verbatims) | Countries (verbatims) | Engines (verbatims) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 | A 2,128 | GB 1,293, **JP 672**, SE 71, FR 53, AU 16, FI 8, DK 8, KR 4 | ICE 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~30–40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.

You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. When a page's job is to hold records that people or Claude will add to or change later — a tracker, a sign-up sheet, a log, a dashboard's numbers — Claude gives the page this database (the `db` capability, via the `artifact-capabilities` skill) instead of writing the records into the page source or browser storage, and later adds or changes rows with `ArtifactData` rather than republishing the page.

**Separate tools**: Claude handles comment threads on a published artifact with `ArtifactComments` and an artifact's shared database with `ArtifactData`, whose actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` or `write_db`. Claude loads either tool when it needs it, and if one appears only as a deferred tool's name, Claude loads it the way this session loads deferred tools before calling it.

**Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

"""The only path to OpenAI (D-014, D-015, D-020). Every call is reserved, logged and settled."""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Literal

import openai
from pydantic import BaseModel

from bmw_req.config import get_settings
from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import budget

Tier = Literal["fast", "smart"]
FLEX_TIMEOUT_S = 900.0


@dataclass
class LLMResult:
    text: str
    parsed: Any
    usage_id: int | None     # None on a cache hit
    cost_usd: float
    response: Any            # None on a cache hit
    cached: bool = False


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, conn=None, client=None):
        self.settings = get_settings()
        self.conn = conn if conn is not None else connect()
        self.client = client if client is not None else openai.OpenAI(api_key=self.settings.openai_api_key)

    def model_for(self, tier: Tier) -> str:
        return {"fast": self.settings.model_fast, "smart": self.settings.model_smart}[tier]

    def generate(
        self,
        *,
        job: str,
        tier: Tier,
        input: str | list,
        max_output_tokens: int,
        instructions: str | None = None,
        schema: type[BaseModel] | None = None,
        reasoning_effort: str | None = None,
        tools: list | None = None,
        max_tool_calls: int | None = None,
        flex: bool = False,
        demo: bool = False,
        use_cache: bool = True,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> LLMResult:
        """Call the Responses API. `schema` → structured output parsed into that Pydantic model.

        Identical requests are served from `llm_cache` for free (D-010) unless use_cache=False.
        """
        if not max_output_tokens or max_output_tokens <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_output_tokens is required on every call (D-014)")
        if tools and not max_tool_calls:
            raise ValueError("Calls with tools need max_tool_calls (D-014 web-search cap)")
        model = self.model_for(tier)
        key = _cache_key(model, instructions, input, schema, reasoning_effort, tools, max_tool_calls, max_output_tokens, kwargs)
        if use_cache:
            hit = self.conn.execute("SELECT output_text FROM llm_cache WHERE key = ?", (key,)).fetchone()
            if hit is not None:
                text = hit["output_text"]
                parsed = schema.model_validate_json(text) if schema is not None else None
                return LLMResult(text=text, parsed=parsed, usage_id=None, cost_usd=0.0, response=None, cached=True)
        prompt_text = (instructions or "") + (input if isinstance(input, str) else json.dumps(input, default=str))
        reserved = budget.worst_case_usd(
            model, budget.estimate_tokens(prompt_text), max_output_tokens, max_tool_calls or 0
        )
        usage_id = budget.reserve(self.conn, job=job, kind="responses", model=model, reserved_usd=reserved, demo=demo)

        params: dict[str, Any] = dict(model=model, input=input, max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens, **kwargs)
        if instructions:
            params["instructions"] = instructions
        if reasoning_effort:
            params["reasoning"] = {"effort": reasoning_effort}
        if tools:
            params["tools"] = tools
            params["max_tool_calls"] = max_tool_calls
        if flex:
            params["service_tier"] = "flex"
            params["timeout"] = FLEX_TIMEOUT_S

        try:
            if schema is not None:
                response = self.client.responses.parse(text_format=schema, **params)
            else:
                response = self.client.responses.create(**params)
        except (openai.APIStatusError, openai.APIConnectionError) as e:
            # Request rejected or never reached the API: not billed.
            budget.settle(self.conn, usage_id, status="failed", cost_usd=0.0, error=repr(e)[:2000])
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            # Response may have been billed (e.g. structured-output parse failure): keep the worst case.
            budget.settle(self.conn, usage_id, status="failed", cost_usd=reserved, error=repr(e)[:2000])
            raise

        u = response.usage
        tier_used = getattr(response, "service_tier", None)
        counts = dict(
            input_tokens=u.input_tokens,
            cached_tokens=u.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens or 0,
            cache_write_tokens=getattr(u.input_tokens_details, "cache_write_tokens", 0) or 0,
            output_tokens=u.output_tokens,
            search_calls=sum(1 for item in response.output if item.type == "web_search_call"),
        )
        cost = budget.actual_usd(model, flex=tier_used == "flex", **counts)
        budget.settle(
            self.conn,
            usage_id,
            status="completed",
            cost_usd=cost,
            service_tier=tier_used,
            reasoning_tokens=u.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens or 0,
            response_id=response.id,
            **counts,
        )
        if getattr(response, "status", "completed") == "completed":
            self.conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO llm_cache (key, job, model, output_text, llm_usage_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (key, job, model, response.output_text, usage_id),
            )
        return LLMResult(
            text=response.output_text,
            parsed=getattr(response, "output_parsed", None),
            usage_id=usage_id,
            cost_usd=cost,
            response=response,
        )

    def embed(self, texts: list[str], *, job: str, demo: bool = False) -> list[list[float]]:
        model = self.settings.model_embed
        reserved = budget.worst_case_usd(model, sum(budget.estimate_tokens(t) for t in texts))
        usage_id = budget.reserve(self.conn, job=job, kind="embeddings", model=model, reserved_usd=reserved, demo=demo)
        try:
            response = self.client.embeddings.create(model=model, input=texts)
        except Exception as e:
            budget.settle(self.conn, usage_id, status="failed", cost_usd=0.0, error=repr(e)[:2000])
            raise
        tokens = response.usage.prompt_tokens
        cost = budget.actual_usd(model, input_tokens=tokens)
        budget.settle(self.conn, usage_id, status="completed", cost_usd=cost, input_tokens=tokens)
        return [d.embedding for d in response.data]


def _cache_key(model, instructions, input, schema, reasoning_effort, tools, max_tool_calls, max_output_tokens, extra) -> str:
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "instructions": instructions,
        "input": input,
        "schema": schema.model_json_schema() if schema is not None else None,
        "reasoning_effort": reasoning_effort,
        "tools": tools,
        "max_tool_calls": max_tool_calls,
        "max_output_tokens": max_output_tokens,
        "extra": extra,
    }
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()

from bmw_req.llm.budget import BudgetExceeded
from bmw_req.llm.client import LLM, LLMResult

__all__ = ["LLM", "LLMResult", "BudgetExceeded"]

        tokens = response.usage.prompt_tokens
        cost = budget.actual_usd(model, input_tokens=tokens)
        budget.settle(self.conn, usage_id, status="completed", cost_usd=cost, input_tokens=tokens)
        return [d.embedding for d in response.data]


def _cache_key(model, instructions, input, schema, reasoning_effort, tools, max_tool_calls, max_output_tokens, extra) -> str:
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "instructions": instructions,
        "input": input,
        "schema": schema.model_json_schema() if schema is not None else None,
        "reasoning_effort": reasoning_effort,
        "tools": tools,
        "max_tool_calls": max_tool_calls,
        "max_output_tokens": max_output_tokens,
        "extra": extra,
    }
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()

def reserve(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, job: str, kind: str, model: str, reserved_usd: float, demo: bool) -> int:
    """Insert a reservation row, or raise BudgetExceeded if it would cross a threshold."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")

"""Ingest `sales_volumes.xlsx` (data-inventory §3).

Per sheet row two `source_item`s (kind 'sales'): the 2024 actual (wave 1) and 2025 actual + 2030 forecast
(wave 2), each referenced by its `sales` rows. Values look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015):
BMW-internal relative weights only, never blended with public figures.
Idempotent: refs already ingested are skipped.

`uv run python -m bmw_req.ingest.sales`
"""

import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

from bmw_req.ingest.common import audit_batch, existing_refs, open_batch

FILE = "sales_volumes.xlsx"

# Config, not code paths (AGENTS rule 7).
# Sheet → vehicle model per file market code ('*' = all other markets). G60_G68 is one combined sheet;
# China is the long-wheelbase G68 (data-inventory §3).
SHEET_MODELS = {
    "F70": {"*": "F70"},
    "G60_G68": {"CN": "G68", "*": "G60"},
    "G70": {"*": "G70"},
}
# File market code → our market code.
MARKET_CODES = {"EU": "EU", "US": "US", "CN": "CN", "RoW": "RoW", "ROW": "RoW"}
# Year column → (wave, is_forecast). Source items group years by wave.
YEARS = {"volume_2024": (2024, 1, 0), "volume_2025": (2025, 2, 0), "volume_2030": (2030, 2, 1)}
NOTE = ("Values look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015) — use as BMW-internal relative weights; "
        "never blend with public sales figures.")


def read_sales(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """One dict per sheet row with cached values; formulas are kept in `formulas` for provenance."""
    wb_val = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    wb_raw = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=False)
    rows = []
    try:
        for sheet, models in SHEET_MODELS.items():
            ws, ws_raw = wb_val[sheet], wb_raw[sheet]
            header = [c.value for c in ws[1]]
            col = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(header) if name}
            for r_idx in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
                cells = [c.value for c in ws[r_idx]]
                code = cells[col["market_code"]]
                if code is None:
                    continue
                if code not in MARKET_CODES:
                    raise ValueError(f"{sheet} row {r_idx}: unknown market code {code!r}")
                market = MARKET_CODES[code]
                formulas = {}
                volumes = {}
                for ycol in YEARS:
                    raw = ws_raw.cell(row=r_idx, column=col[ycol] + 1).value
                    if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.startswith("="):
                        formulas[ycol] = raw
                    v = cells[col[ycol]]
                    volumes[ycol] = int(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float)) else None
                rows.append({
                    "sheet": sheet, "row": r_idx, "market_label": cells[col["market"]], "file_code": code,
                    "market": market, "model": models.get(code, models["*"]), "volumes": volumes,
                    "formulas": formulas,
                })
    finally:
        wb_val.close()
        wb_raw.close()
    return rows


def _items(path_name: str, row: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Split a row into one source item per wave."""
    by_wave: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
    for ycol, (_, wave, _) in YEARS.items():
        by_wave.setdefault(wave, []).append(ycol)
    out = []
    for wave, ycols in sorted(by_wave.items()):
        years = [YEARS[c][0] for c in ycols]
        suffix = "+".join(str(y) for y in years)
        parts = [f"{y}{' (forecast)' if YEARS[c][2] else ''}: {row['volumes'][c]:,} units"
                 if row["volumes"][c] is not None else f"{y}: n/a" for c, y in zip(ycols, years)]
        out.append({
            "ref": f"{path_name}#{row['sheet']}:R{row['row']}:{suffix}",
            "wave": wave,
            "ycols": ycols,
            "text": f"BMW sales volumes, {row['model']} {row['market']} ({row['market_label']}) — " + "; ".join(parts)
                    + " (BMW-internal, stylized; Q-015)",
            "meta": {
                "sheet": row["sheet"], "excel_row": row["row"], "market_label": row["market_label"],
                "file_market_code": row["file_code"], "years": years,
                "volumes": {str(YEARS[c][0]): row["volumes"][c] for c in ycols},
                "formulas": {c: f for c, f in row["formulas"].items() if c in ycols},
                "combined_sheet": row["sheet"] if len(SHEET_MODELS[row["sheet"]]) > 1 else None,
                "notes": NOTE,
            },
        })
    return out


def ingest_sales(conn: sqlite3.Connection, path: Path) -> int:
    """Returns the number of newly ingested source items."""
    path = Path(path)
    rows = read_sales(path)
    seen = existing_refs(conn, "sales", path.name)
    todo = [(row, it) for row in rows for it in _items(path.name, row) if it["ref"] not in seen]
    if not todo:
        return 0
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        batch_id = open_batch(conn, "sales", f"{len(todo)} sales items from {path.name}", path.name)
        n_sales = 0
        for row, it in todo:
            sid = conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
                                            text, meta_json, ingest_batch_id, wave)
                   VALUES ('sales', ?, ?, 'T1', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (it["ref"], f"{row['sheet']}:{row['file_code']}", row["model"], row["market"], it["text"],
                 json.dumps(it["meta"]), batch_id, it["wave"]),
            ).lastrowid
            for ycol in it["ycols"]:
                year, _, forecast = YEARS[ycol]
                conn.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO sales (vehicle_model_id, market_code, year, units, is_forecast, source_item_id)
                       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                    (row["model"], row["market"], year, row["volumes"][ycol], forecast, sid),
                )
                n_sales += 1
        audit_batch(conn, "ingest.sales", batch_id,
                    {"file": path.name, "source_items": len(todo), "sales_rows": n_sales, "note": NOTE})
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return len(todo)


def main() -> None:
    from bmw_req.config import get_settings
    from bmw_req.db import connect
    from bmw_req.ingest import reference

    conn = connect()
    reference.seed(conn)
    path = get_settings().raw_data_dir / FILE
    rows = read_sales(path)
    print("market codes in file:", sorted({r["file_code"] for r in rows}))
    for r in rows:
        if r["formulas"]:
            print(f"  formula cells {r['sheet']} R{r['row']}: {r['formulas']} → cached {r['volumes']}")
    print(f"sales: {ingest_sales(conn, path)} new source items")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
